title: Private min pack: add control plane health dashboards (policy/config + auth integration)
author: Sergio Costa
description:
Adds baseline Grafana dashboards for Redwood Private control plane services so operators can quickly diagnose config/policy rollout issues and auth integration regressions without bespoke queries. This is part of the Private observability minimum pack; these dashboards follow the same folder/naming/templating conventions established in PRs #318–#323.

Dashboards included (Grafana): (1) "Private / Control Plane / Policy & Config" (primary audience: oncall operator / SRE). Panels cover API request rate/latency/error for policy-service + config-service, reconciliation/rollout loop health, policy evaluation failures (deny vs error), config apply latency, and dependency signals (store connectivity, leader election, request timeouts). (2) "Private / Control Plane / Auth & Identity" (primary audience: operator / security engineer). Panels cover auth-gateway request rate/latency/error, OIDC/JWKS refresh health, token validation failures by reason, upstream IdP connectivity (HTTP status), and RBAC/authz decision errors. Where metrics are not yet emitted consistently across all private installs, panels are written to fail "soft" (showing empty series rather than query errors) and include a "missing signals" text panel that points to the minimum signals standard.

Implementation notes: - Uses the shared templating library (cluster/namespace/environment/instance variables) and a consistent datasource reference ("Prometheus") to remain compatible with provisioning defaults. - Avoids any panels that might inadvertently surface secrets/PII; metrics are aggregated and do not include token/user identifiers. - Uses label joins sparingly and avoids high-cardinality dimensions (no request_id, no raw principal). - Adds annotations for deploy/upgrade windows when present (re-uses the same annotation key as other min-pack dashboards).

Known gaps / follow-ups: - Some auth integration panels assume the control plane exports JWKS refresh counters and token validation error reasons; if a customer is on older private builds, those panels will be empty (expected). - Runbook links are placeholders; Docs workstream will wire these to Confluence pages.

Test plan: - Compiled dashboards via jsonnet build and validated against Grafana dashboard schema in CI. - Smoke-loaded dashboards in staging VPC reference env; verified variable dropdowns populate and queries execute with Prometheus 2.49 + Grafana 10.2.

Checklist: [x] Dashboard JSON validated in CI [x] Folder + UID naming follows min-pack conventions [x] Queries avoid high-cardinality labels [x] Security review: no sensitive fields exposed [x] Added short README notes on required metrics.

Related: PM-612 (initiative), ENG-2841 (repo structure + provisioning framework).

notable_snippets: Example query used for config apply latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, cluster, namespace) (rate(redwood_config_apply_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m])))

Example query used for auth token validation failures (low cardinality): sum by (reason, cluster, namespace) (rate(redwood_auth_token_validation_failures_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]))
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we align variable names and defaults with the gateway/runtime dashboards? Specifically: use $environment and $namespace consistently, and avoid per-pod panels unless behind a toggle. Also please double check label cardinality (reason looks ok, but don't add principal/client_id).

Sergio Costa (author): Updated to use the shared private.libsonnet vars (cluster/namespace/environment). Removed the per-pod table from the default view; added an optional "Instance" variable that is hidden by default. Confirmed token failure reason is an enum and not user-derived.

Marcus Lin (review): Security nit: the "OIDC upstream URL" stat panel is pulling label values. Even if it’s just a host, we should avoid showing raw URLs (customers consider IdP endpoints sensitive). Can you drop it or hash it? Also ensure we’re not displaying error messages coming from upstream.

Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Removed the URL label panel entirely and replaced with status/latency/error-rate panels keyed by integration type only. No error message labels used; only reason enum + HTTP status class (2xx/4xx/5xx).

Ethan Park (review): Useful. Two requests: (1) Add a panel for policy rollout success rate (applied vs failed) and (2) a small panel for dependency connectivity (store client errors) for policy-service. We see "silent" failures when the store is degraded.
Sergio Costa (author): Added rollout success ratio panel and store client errors/timeout panels. Also added a short text panel describing what "rollout" means and where to look when it stalls.
Priya Natarajan (review): Looks aligned with the min pack goals. Thanks for keeping this "day-1 usable" and not overfitting. Approving after CI is green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Sergio Costa (after approvals).
release_notes: Private observability min pack now includes control plane dashboards for policy/config rollout health and auth/identity integration health (Grafana).
